success_patterns: First-turn requests with a missing mandatory date (flight with only a purpose such as 'wedding' or 'birthday', hotel with 'last-minute' and a party size, round-trip flight plus hotel with no dates) produced a single short seek_information naming only the missing items and made no search call. This is already covered by the DATE GATE, Rule 6 and Rule 7.

Hotel refinements with 'hotels' and 'restaurants' both cached (budget plus business center; 'At least 3 stars') loaded only the hotels key and passed only the last turn's new kwargs, in the correct shapes (stars=[3, 5], has_business_center=True). This is covered by Rules 0, 13, 17 and 27 and by Strategic Guidance A and B.

A bare 'Yes, that sounds wonderful' accepting a new attraction type (Scenic) triggered a fresh search_attractions(city=..., type=[...]) saved as 'attractions'. It did not touch the flight or hotel keys that were also cached. This is covered by Strategic Guidance C and Rule 10.
Every search or filter call was assigned to a variable and followed by save_to_cache, with no imports or comments. This is covered by the HARD OUTPUT RULES.

patch.reasoning: Every behavior in these eight successes is already encoded in the skill: the date gate and seek_information rules, minimal one-domain hotel filters, accepting a new attraction type with a fresh search, and output hygiene. The meta-skill warns against adding sibling examples or growing the skill by accretion, so I propose no edits. One note: Trajectory 1 ('Not really' with attractions cached) passed on cache_em even though the agent re-searched instead of reading the cache. That is a lenient metric, not a pattern to reinforce.
